A period of freezing rain occurred, then winds shifted sharply to the south at 940pm, gusting 30-40mph, the temperature spiking up 20 degrees and changing to rain. The SNOTEL site at Moore Creek rose above freezing closer to 11pm, so estimated that freezing rain continued up the Klondike Highway until then.||At 1013am on the 9th, the Skagway police shared that the Klondike Highway would remain closed due to low visibility. The police advised at 826pm to refrain from driving the Dyea Road unless an absolute emergency due to several slides covering the roadway. The police also noted that all roads in Skagway were experiencing heavy snow cover and should be avoided as well. The Skagway COOP measured 10 inches of snow the following morning, but likely saw significant melt/compaction.

Just over 5 inches of snow had fallen across the downtown Haines area as of 8am on the 4th based on the COOP and CoCoRaHS stations. After a lull in snowfall until around noon, rates picked up again becoming heavy in the evening with NW winds sustained winds increasing to around 20 mph at the airport with higher gusts near Lynn Canal. The CoCoRaHS spotter in the Skyline Drive area reported blowing snow and a new accumulation of 6.5 inches by 910pm on the 4th. By 8am on the 5th, the same location had a new 24hr total of 12.9 inches of snow with snow continuing to fall. The COOP in town, at a lower elevation, measured a 24hr snowfall of 8.9 inches. Snow tapered off through the evening of the 5th as temperatures warmed and new snowfall measurements the following morning were just over 5 inches with a glaze of freezing rain. The COOP station at Haines Customs reported considerably less snow during this period with less than 2 inches each day.

A trained spotter in Gustavus reported periods of snow through the 4th, but with snowfall rates increasing at 8pm in the evening and a new snow accumulation of 6.5 inches falling during the overnight period to 730am on the 5th. Moderate to heavy snow fell through the morning of the 5th with mixing then a change over to rain in town by around 1pm and around 3pm at the Glacier Bay National Park. Snowfall accumulations at the park were missing for the morning of the 5th but with a snow depth increase of 13 inches and heavy snow falling at the time.

The Marine Exchange of Alaska observation at the Skagway Ore Dock measured the first high wind gust as winds shifted suddenly out of the south with a peak of 56.4kt (65mph) at 230pm on the 6th. The Skagway Airport ASOS measured a peak gust of 55kt (63mph) at 415pm and the Marine Exchange station at the harbor measured a peak gust of 51.8kt (60mph) at 714pm. High wind gusts continued into the night at the Airport until 1104pm and at the Ore Dock until 123am.

The local Gustavus DOT official reported large trees coming down with branches blocking the road in the 2pm hour on the 7th. Other spotters confirmed a large tree down across the NPS road and another large tree down near Four Corners. Near the 3pm high tide, waves were observed cresting at the upper edge of the ferry staging island. ||The Marine Exchange station on the road to the Ferry Terminal measured a peak wind gust of 52.8kt (61mph) at 307pm after winds shifted from SE to SW. The Gustavus Airport AWOS noted the wind shift at 204pm and measured a peak gust of 40kt (46mph) at 325pm. Bartlett Cove also had a peak gust of 46mph an hour later.

The Marine Exchange station at George Island measured peak wind gusts in excess of 60mph after winds shifted to the WSW with the front between 133pm and 312pm AKST on March 7th. This included a peak gust of 66.9kt (77mph) at 152pm. The Marine Exchange station in Pelican also observed a peak gust that hour, reaching 56.2kt (65mph) at 151pm AKST. Observations from Elfin Cove were not available during this event.

Periodic snow showers fell on the 8th, then became steady around 5pm AKDT with periods of heavy rates through the night, particularly over North Douglas Island and areas just south of the airport. By 5am AKDT on the 9th, a report on North Douglas had at least 8 inches of snow in the previous 12 hours. An NWS employee in the same area measured 12 inches of accumulation between 9pm and 6am AKDT. A report from the Lemon Creek area also had nearly 12 inches by 745am AKDT. Snow showers continued through mid day on the 9th, then rates decreased. Other parts of the Juneau zone, particularly north of the airport had much lighter snowfall accumulations from these showers reaching just over 4 inches at the NWS Office and less than 2 inches at Lena Point.

A trained spotter in Craig, on the SW side of Prince of Wales Island, measured 5 inches of snow between 8pm on the 10th to 133am on the 11th and another 2 inches by 343am AKDT. The COOP observer in Craig measured a 24hr total of 11 inches at 845am AKDT with moderate snow showers continuing and another 3.2 inches the following morning. The COOP in Klawock measured 9 inches of new snow at 9am AKST while the COOP in Thorne Bay on the eastern side of the island only measured 2.5 inches.

Periodic snow showers fell over Yakutat during the evening of the 14th, then rates increased and became steady after about 1am AKDT on the 15th. Visibility periodically fell to a quarter mile through the morning with around 7 inches of snowfall accumulation measured by 1pm when snow let up.

Snow began at the Ketchikan Airport around 850am AKDT on the 15th while the COOP at the northern end of the borough noted snow began around 730am. The wind was already picking up at the airport in the morning with gusts of 20-30mph. Theses gusts continued to increase through the day while snow continued. The strongest winds of the day occurred within the 4pm hour with the Marine Exchange station at Salmon Landing reaching a peak gust of 62 mph at 435pm. Other wind gusts with this system across Ketchikan ranged from 40-56mph.  A social media report from 7 mile South Tongass Highway noted 6.5 inches of heavy and wet snow had fallen. A trained spotter near downtown Ketchikan reported 6.5 inches of snow as well by 6pm AKDT and the airport reported a change to rain shortly after this. The COOP at the northern end of town saw only 1.8 inches of snow and was already mixing at their 3pm report time.

Snow began across Prince of Wales Island around 7am on the 15th based on a CoCoRaHS report from Edna Bay and DOT RWIS webcams showing accumulation on the highways. The wind was already picking up at observation points on the SW side of the island including peak gusts of 50-56mph in the late afternoon between Craig and Hydaburg. The wind caused temperatures to steadily rise across the south with an early change over to rain and snowfall amounts near sea level of less than 2 inches. However, the snowfall was able to accumulate more across the north and at elevation. The CoCoRaHS report from Edna Bay at 7am the following morning measured 6 inches of snow and based on nearby temperatures, likely changed to rain around 7pm the night before, making this a 12 hour snowfall measurement.

Snow showers fell across the Chilkat Peninsula early on the 15th with advisory level rates. After a break, steady snowfall began again in the evening and ending during the morning of the 16th. The morning 511 report from DOT estimated that 4 to 8 inches of snow had fallen along the Haines Highway by 430am with difficult travel conditions. The COOP report from Haines Customs measured much less at 1.5 inches the morning of the 16th and the COOP in town measured 3.8 inches.

Light snow began in Hyder around noon local time on Sunday the 15th then rates increased overnight with visibility down to a half mile at times at the nearby Stewart B.C. weather station. A trained spotter in Hyder reported 11 inches of snow had fallen by 8am AKDT with snow continuing. The same spotter had another 6 inches by 2pm AKDT and topped out at of total of 18.5 inches when it had begun to change to rain around 630pm AKDT the evening of the 16th.

A spotter in Pelican reported around 10 inches of snow had fallen on the 18th and another 2 inches overnight into the morning of the 19th for an estimated 12 inches in a 24 hour period. Timing of the snowfall start/stop times based on other nearby observation stations.
Gustavus airport ASOS measured temperatures below freezing between 11 PM AKST Monday October 6th and 10 AM Tuesday October 7th. The lowest temperature recorded was 26F.

Temperatures went below freezing as measured at Hoonah Airport AWOS during the morning of Tuesday 10/07 between midnight and 9 AM AKST. The minimum temperature recorded was 29F. Outlying areas were estimated to have temperatures in the lower 20s.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Juneau airport ASOS measured temperatures below freezing from 11 PM AKST on the night of 10/6 through 10 AM AKST 10/7. The minimum temperature recorded was 26F.

events.cz_name: CAPE FAIRWEATHER TO CAPE SUCKLING COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The Yakutat AWOS measured below freezing temperatures for several hours between 1 AM and 5 AM on the morning of 10/9. The minimum temperature recorded was 29F. Outlying areas from town had colder temperatures.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Hydaburg AWOS measured several wind gusts at 49 KT during the evening of 10/21. Gusts were estimated around Craig at 60 KT on the night of 10/21. Klawock Airport ASOS also had a measured gust to 49 KT at midnight 10/22.

Trained spotters at Thorne Bay and Meyers Chuck estimated 65 KT during the night of 10/21 into the morning of 10/22. Marine reports showed even higher gusts. The Annette ASOS measured a peak wind 55 KT at 2153 AKST on 10/21. No damage was reported.

Based on pressure gradients from NCEP analyses and surface observations in Zone 28, wind speeds in excess of 65 KT occurred on the night of 10/21 for the western areas of the Misty Fjords. No damage was reported.

events.cz_name: CAPE DECISION TO SALISBURY SOUND COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Sitka airport ASOS had peak winds 49 KT around 1600 to 1700 AKST on 10/28. NCEP analyses indicted that strong pressure gradients at that time caused winds across headlands in excess of 70 MPH.
The Haines COOP observer measured 13 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending 0800 AKST 10/29.

events.cz_name: CAPE DECISION TO SALISBURY SOUND COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Sitka ASOS had a peak wind of 60 MPH at 0153 AKST 10/22. Numerous gusts were observed there in the 50 MPH range. NCEP Analyses showed such strong surface pressure gradients that headland winds could have been as high as 80 MPH on 10/22.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Although the wind speeds at Elfin Cove were not significant on 10/22, Cape Spencer observed a peak wind of 74 KT at 0400 AKST on 10/22 and very strong winds continued throughout the day there. It is estimated that the winds along headlands and channeled terrain were around 75 MPH during this event.

Skagway ASOS reported a wind gust 53 MPH at 1353 AKST on 10/22. White Pass had estimated gusts to 70 MPH around the same time, and a marine observation, Eldred Rock in Lynn Canal had a peak wind of 61 KT at 1700 AKST on 10/22.

Haines customs measured 21.0 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 0700 AKST 11/2. Haines cooperative observer downtown measured 8.6 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 0800 on 11/2.
Haines Customs measured 6.0 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 0800 AKST 11/15. Analyses showed that the snow began around midnight and was heavy by 0400 AKST.
Frequent wind gusts 60-75 MPH occurred late on the night of 12/20 into the daytime hours 12/21 at the Skagway Airport ASOS. No damage was reported.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: The Juneau South Douglas wind profiler measured peak surface winds 60 to to 71 MPH on the morning of 12/21. No damage was reported during this Taku wind type event.

events.cz_name: CAPE FAIRWEATHER TO CAPE SUCKLING COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The NWS office in Yakutat measured 2.4 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at midnight 12/4 and 7.2 inches for 24 hours ending at midnight 12/5. Most of the snow fell between 2100 AKST 12/3 and noon 12/4 for a storm total of 9.6 inches snowfall.

Heavy snow began at the Gustavus Airport around midnight 12/4. The Glacier Bay coop observer measured 11.0 inches new snow for 24 hours ending at 0800 AKST 12/4. All of this snowfall was after midnight. The Gustavus coop observer had 7.2 inches ending at 0700 AKST 12/4.

The Hyder coop observer was away for the month of December, 2008. Observations at Stewart, British Columbia, indicated that constant heavy snow fell on the night of 12/4 and all day 12/5. It is estimated that 1 to 2 feet of snow fell during that period.

events.cz_name: CAPE FAIRWEATHER TO CAPE SUCKLING COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: In the middle of a significant snow storm, the Cape Suckling buoy indicated a strong east wind for the western part of the area starting around 1500 AKST on 12/8. Several gusts to 52 KT were observed there and the NCEP analysis at 2100 AKST showed that strong winds did occur over land west of Icy Bay.

events.cz_name: CAPE FAIRWEATHER TO CAPE SUCKLING COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The NWS office in Yakutat measured 5.2 inches of new snowfall during the evening of 12/8 and 4.0 inches of new snow between 0000 and 0600 AKST on 12/9 for a storm total of 9.2 inches in 12 hours.

In the early morning hours of 12/9, the Klondike Highway had blizzard conditions as extrapolated from the observations at the Skagway Airport. 4 inches of new snow fell on 12/9 at the power plant while frequent winds to 35 MPH occurred toward the pass. By the persistent visibility of 1 mile in snow and blowing snow in town, the Klondike Highway certainly had white out conditions throughout the day on 12/9.

Haines Customs had 18.0 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at 0800 on 12/9 and 7.0 inches ending at at 0800 on 12/10. This storm was also a blizzard with white out conditions, plus blowing and drifting snow in 35 MPH winds.

Haines Customs had 18.0 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at 0800 on 12/9 and 7.0 inches ending at at 0800 on 12/10. This storm was also a blizzard with white out conditions, plus blowing and drifting snow in 35 MPH winds.
The cooperative observer at Hoonah measured 9.8 inches of new snow between 0200 and 0800 AKST 12/9.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Juneau had one of the worst snowstorms of the season on 12/9. The cooperative observer at mile 17 measured 17.8 inches of new snowfall at 0700 AKST on 12/9. Snow did not begin until the evening of 12/8 and heavy snow was not observed at the airport until late. A peak wind of 30 MPH was observed at the airport on 12/9 which had 10.7 inches of new snow. Most recorded amounts were in the 10 to 15 inches range.

events.cz_name: CAPE DECISION TO SALISBURY SOUND COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The outer coast had winds around 60 MPH late on the night of 12/8 and during the early morning hours of 12/9. Although the Sitka airport only had 47 MPH, NCEP analysis showed strong surface pressure gradients which certainly caused headland winds to 60 MPH ahead of the front.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The Hydaburg seaplane base observed gusts to 51 KT at 2236 AKST on 12/9. Coastal headlands probably had wind speeds to 75 MPH at that time.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The automated observation at Cape Spencer indicated that quite a wind storm persisted along the outer coast from the night of 12/8 well into 12/10. E wind with gusts estimated at 65 KT shifted to SW then W that Tuesday.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Pelican measured 7.4 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at 0700 AKST on 12/24. Analyses showed that the heavy snow fell between 1700 and 2300 on 12/23.

events.cz_name: CAPE DECISION TO SALISBURY SOUND COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Little Port Walter measured 10.2 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at 1700 AKST on 12/23 and another 6.3 inches on 12/24. No snow measurements were available for Sitka.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow was observed with less than 1/4 mile visibility at 0500 AKST with 3.0 inches of new snow. Unfortunately no further measurements were made that day in the entire area, but it is estimated that the Hollis highway received about one foot of new snow early on 12/24.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The Pelican cooperative observer measured 7.4 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 0800 AKST 12/24. Analyses showed that the snow fell between midnight and 0600 early on the morning of the 12/24.

events.cz_name: CAPE FAIRWEATHER TO CAPE SUCKLING COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The Yakutat office measured 6.5 inches of new snow during the evening of 12/25, then 15.9 inches of new additional snow midnight to midnight on 12/26. During the early morning of 12/27, Yakutat measured an additional 1.7 inches of new snow. Outlying areas were estimated to have received even greater amounts.

The Klondike Highway had heavy snow on 12/26 with near blizzard conditions with blowing and drifting snow. The snowfall had low liquid content which made measurements nearly impossible with wind gusts to 37 MPH. The customs tried to measure and got 4.2 inches new on 12/26. It was estimated that well over a foot fell in this storm. ASOS observations at the airport showed that the snow persisted into 12/27.

The town of Haines was buried in this event. The downtown cooperative observer measured 17.3 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 0800 on 12/26 and 12.7 inches of new snow on 12/27. Plows were busy with 30 inches of snow to remove.

Glacier Bay cooperative observer measured 6.5 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at 0800 AKST on 10/26. This snow fell the previous night. Glacier Bay had 10.0 inches new on 12/27 ending at 0800. Gustavus airport AWOS showed that the heaviest snow ended on the afternoon of 10/26.
Hoonah did not get much snow during this storm. Tenakee Springs did not report. Hidden Falls hatchery to the south of the area got 13 inches of new snow in 24 hours ending at 1700 AKST on 12/26.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The Gulf coast around Cross Sound got buried in snow with this storm. The cooperative observer at Pelican measured 7.0 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 0800 AKST 12/26, 9.0 inches new on 12/27. Additionally a snow advisory was issued for 12/28 and 10.0 inches new resulted. Storm total was 26 inches with 32 inches on the ground at the end of the storm.

events.cz_name: EASTERN BARANOF ISLAND AND SOUTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Hidden Falls hatchery measured 13.0 inches of new snow in 24 hours ending at 1700 AKST on 12/26.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Trained spotters ranged from storm totals of 8 to 19 inches new snow for 12/26 through 12/28. The airport measured 11.2 inches. The Forecast Office measured a storm total of 8.5 inches and Lemmon creek had 9.7 inches.

events.cz_name: INNER CHANNELS FROM KUPREANOF ISLAND TO ETOLIN ISLAND
events.event_narrative: A trained spotter measured a storm total of 11.0 inches new snow for 24 hours ending at 0800 AKST on 12/27. Petersburg airport got 12.5 inches 12/26 through 12/28 from this storm. The heaviest snow occurred on Friday, 12/26. Wrangell measured 6.0 inches on 12/26.

The Hyder NWS cooperative observer was not available for December. Based on analyses and observations of heavy snow at Stewart, British Columbia, it was estimated that over a foot of new snow fell during this storm.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The trained spotter in Craig measured 4.6 inches of new snow at 0800 AKST on 12/28. Analyses showed that the snowfall occurred overnight and police reported that higher amounts occurred around the island estimated to be around 8 inches along with wind to 40 MPH. The Holis to Craig road received the most snow.
The Ketchikan area got buried by persistent snow on 12/28. Storm totals from spotters ranged from a low of 8.0 inches to 17.8 inches of new snow on that day.

Light to moderate snowfall combined with very strong winds with sustained 30 to 40 mph with gusts of 50 to 70 mph, reduced visibilities to near zero for periods of times along the Klondike Highway and in Skagway.||Local storm reports:||0930 AM     Blizzard         8 N Skagway             59.57N 135.33W|01/04/2009                                      AK   CO-OP Observer  ||            Skagway customs reporting 1/8 mi visibility in blowing |            snow. Estimated wind speed 35 MPH with higher gusts. |            Temperature 4 below zero. Light to moderate snowfall leading up to and through the event.  Strong sustained north winds to 25 mph with gusts of 35 to 50 mph...and locally stronger along Lynn Canal south of Haines, reduced visibilites to near zero for several periods during the afternoon and evening.

events.cz_name: INNER CHANNELS FROM KUPREANOF ISLAND TO ETOLIN ISLAND
events.event_narrative: A frontal band moved onshore southeast the night of 3 Jan, developing an overrunning snow event for the central and southern panhandle into the following afternoon. It began to snow heavily over the northern portions of Kupreanof Island. A spotter reported the morning of the 4th that they had received 5.75 inches of snow in 12 hours at Petersburg. Total snow fall in Petersburg for the event was 7.5 inches.

events.cz_name: EASTERN BARANOF ISLAND AND SOUTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: A frontal band moved onshore over Southeast Alaska the night of 3 Jan, developing an overrunning snow event for the central and southern panhandle starting early on the 3rd into the following afternoon. Hidden Falls, a CO-OP station on eastern Baranof Island reported, for roughly a 60 hour period ending at 05/1700 they received 35.1 inches of snow.  The bulk of the snow fell from the evening of the 3rd to 4th.

A frontal band moved onshore over Southeast the night of 3 Jan, developing an overrunning snow event for the central and southern panhandle into the following afternoon. The heavier snow started early in the evening on the 3rd and persisted into the following morning with slowly warming temperatures that changed the snow over to rain late in the morning hours. Annette Weather Service Office reported a snow total of 6 inches, with a spotter about 12 miles north of Ketchikan reported a total of 7 inches before it changed to rain.

A frontal band moved onshore over Southeast the night of 3 Jan, developing an overrunning snow event for the central and southern panhandle into the following afternoon. It began to snow heavily the afternoon the 3rd and persisted into the morning of the 5th. Hidden Inlet CO-OP reported 16.4 inches the morning of the 4th with an additional 10.6 inches /27 inch storm total/ for the event. Stewart BC right across the border from Hyder reported 19.7 inches for roughly the same time.
Snow showers moving onshore after a low had moved into central British Columbia persisted overnight. A public spotter report in Hyder of 14 inches of snowfall over the interior valleys.

A strong front moved across the panhandle overnight with very gusty winds of 60 mph with some to 80 mph between 3 am and 4 am AKST the 30th. The storm knocked out power in the Ketchikan area briefly overnight.  Alaska State Ferry LITUYA, a 180-foot vessel, broke free from its mooring in Metlakatla, Alaska, was adrift in Port Chester, and had grounded on Scrub Island.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: A strong front moved across the panhandle overnight with very gusty winds to 64 mph at Hydaburg at 11:56 pm the 30th. There were several spotter reports as well with gusts of 50 to 60 mph.  Reports of a few trees down on the road.

events.cz_name: CAPE DECISION TO SALISBURY SOUND COASTAL AREA

The Hoonah coop measured 8.1 inches of new snow by 9 am. Nearly all of the new snow fell in the 12 hour period leading up to 9 am AKST.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: The over running snow event spread across the area the night of the 2nd and early morning of the 3rd.  Numerous snow total reports in the Juneau area topped 8 inches: Canyon Island in Taku Inlet 15.4 inches and Annex Creek Power station 15.3 inches in 24 hours ending at 9 am, Juneau Forecast Office 10.4 inches overnight, Juneau Airport 9.3 inches overnight, Snettisham Power station reported 8.5 inches overnight,  Fritz Cove Road coop in Juneau 9.0 inches in 9 hours, and West Juneau Coop received 6.0 inches in 9 hours.

An overrunning snow event occurred over the interior valleys of Misty Fjords impacting the town of Hyder. A public report from Hyder of estimated 20 inches of snow between 7 pm the 2nd and noon the 3rd.

The coop station at Skagway Power measured 7.0 inches new snow by 7 am on the 7th. Based on estimates of observations at the Skagway airport, a few miles away, the main snow accumulation was over by 3 am.

A brief overrunning snow event occurred as weak trough moved across the northern panhandle. The heavier snow amounts were limited to the northern portion primarily near the border. The coop at the Haines Customs measured a new snow total of 5.8 inches primarily within 12 hours of 3 AM.

A band of moisture was lifted over the cold arctic air over the northern panhandle resulting in a good overrunning event of moderate to heavy snow.  The coop in Haines reported 13 inches of snow since 8 am at 4 pm.  An event total of 17 inches by 930 pm was reported by the coop.  A spotter 6 miles south of Haines reported an event total of 15 inches of snow. The spotter reported that at least 2 trees were toppled due the weight of the snow.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: An overrunning event occurred over interior valleys leading to the Canadian interior as a weak trough moved over the northern panhandle. The heaviest snow amounts were restricted to the these valleys.  Snettisham Power Station reported a total of 7 inches in the previous 12 hours. Canyon Island in Taku Inlet reported a total of 19.1 inches for a 24 hour total ending the morning of the 7th. A NWS employee estimated a 6 inches snowfall by 1 pm.  The Juneau Forecast Office reported a snow fall of 7.0 inches in 12 hours by 3 pm.

An overrunning snow event occurred with arctic air over the interior valley near Hyder. Based on observations of the Canadian station at Stewart, BC an estimated 12 inches of snow fell in the vicinity of Hyder from early on the 2/7 through that evening.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND

A NWS employee reported 11.0 inches of snow on Douglas Island. A coop at Lemon Creek (in Juneau) reported 9.8 inches of snow in roughly 15 hours. Annex Creek coop reported 17.0 inches of snow for a 24 total.  Canyon Islands 24 hour total was 12.0 inches and Snettisham Power station reported a 24 hour total of 25.0 inches.
The coop in Haines had received 6.9 inches by 8 am on the 10th. An event total of 8.1 inches was recorded by the afternoon of the 10th.
A spotter in Tenakee Springs reported a snowfall total overnight of 8.0 inches overnight.

The coop observer in Hoonah reported that a snowfall of 6.8 inches essentially fell in 9 hours time. As of 8 am the morning of the 3rd another 7.4 inches of snow had fallen. Based on nearby observations the snow ended at midnight on 3 March, which leads to a 24 hour total (midnight to midnight) of 14.4 inches of snow.

A spotter near Haines reported 10.5 inches of snow since the morning hours and at total of 13.2 inches so far for the event at 4 pm.  By 8 pm that night they had received a storm total of 17.1 inches. Haines customs station reported an event total of 13 inches on the morning of the 13th, and the Haines Coop had a 24 hour total of 14 inches. Most of the heavy snow fell during the daytime on the 12th according to an observation site in Haines.

Two coop sites in the Gustavus area reported 8 inches of snow at 7 am and 9 inches at 8 am on 3/12. Based on observations the heavier snow started falling after midnight on the 2nd and snow continued into the afternoon hours in the area although little additional accumulation resulted.

The coop observer in Hoonah reported at snow total at 9 am March 12 of 9.6 inches, and based on estimates from nearby observations sites the heavier snow began after midnight the 12th so the accumulation was in less than 12 hours.  An additional couple of inches were reported during the day on the 12th.

events.event_narrative: Yakutat observed the first hard freeze of the season on the morning of September 29th under clear skies on calm winds. Temperatures ranged below 28F from 0500 to 0700 AKST with a minimum of 26F. This freeze ended the growing season for the Yakutat area.

A low temperature of 28F was observed at the Ketchikan Airport ASOS (PAKT) at 0448 AKST on 10/12. Outlying areas, especially further away from Tongass Narrows, had estimated minimum temperatures to 23F.
The minimum temperature on 10/12 for the Hyder was 29F during the early morning hours. The estimated temperatures for outlying areas were in the lower 20s.
Haines Airport AWOS (PAHN) observed a minimum temperature of 29F on 10/13 during the early morning hours. Outlying areas further from Lynn Canal had estimated minimum temperatures in the lower 20s.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Hydaburg AWOS reported a gust of 63 MPH at 1016 pm on 4 November.
Although Haines received only 4 to 8 inches of snow combined for 11/16 and 11/17, periods of freezing rain frequently occurred during that time along with rain and gusty winds.
The Hoonah public works water plant (COOP) observed 13.5 inches of new snowfall between 0800 AKST and 1730 AKST on 11/16. Snowfall tapered off during the evening hours.

Haines Customs observed 5.6 inches of new snow on the afternoon of 11/23.  It is highly likely there was higher amounts that occurred along the highway in the Chilkat River valley.  Based on observations at the Haines ASOS, the snow mainly fell up the highway during a period of 8 hours or less.

The COOP observer at the Haines Custom station measured 14 inches of new snowfall|for 24 hours ending at 0700 on 11/26. Based on surface observations in the area, the heavier snowfall fell during the day into the next morning. The snowfall was wet and changed to rain the morning of the 26th.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Juneau ASOS reported a gust of 62 mph at the airport. Reports of tree damage in the Mendenhall Valley up to 2 ft diameter.  The sensor on the Juneau Federal Building reported a gust of 63 mph. A wind sensor on top of Sheep Mountain at an elevation about 3000 ft reported a gust of 186 mph. Power outages occurred. This wind was a contributing factor to mudslides the next day due to soil disturbance of root systems.

events.event_narrative: Yakutat ASOS observed several measured gusts of 45 KT during 11/14. Skagway ASOS observed a measured gust of 52 KT at 0848 AKST on 11/14.

events.event_narrative: Sitka ASOS had several peak winds of 49 KT during the afternoon of 11/14. NCEP analyses showed that even stronger headland winds to 80 MPH were possible.
Ketchikan ASOS observed a measured gust of 54 KT at 0853 AKST on 11/14. The Lincoln Rock C-MAN site had peak winds exceeding 99 KT on the morning of 11/14|(marine observation).

Ketchikan ASOS observed a measured gust of 54 KT at 0853 AKST on 11/14. The Lincoln Rock C-MAN site had peak winds exceeding 99 KT on the morning of 11/14|(marine observation).  These winds are estimated to be representative of the western headlands and shores of the Misty Fjords area.
Skagway COOP observer measured 14.0 inches of new snow at 1600 AKST over 24 hours.

Although the snow dumped on the Misty Fjords area, much of the snow was compacted and washed away when mixed or changing to rain. Only 2 inches of snowfall resulted in the town of Hyder, but outlying areas received feet of new snow.

events.cz_name: CAPE FAIRWEATHER TO CAPE SUCKLING COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: WSO Yakutat measured 5.8 inches of new snow at 2353 on the night of 11/30. An additional 0.3 inches fell before 0400 on 12/1 for a storm total of over 6 inches for a few hours around midnight. The snow changed rapidly to rain around 0400 on 12/1 and melted away very quickly.

Based on the observations at Haines Airport, snow began for the area in the early morning hours of 12/16. Heavy accumulations did not occur until the early morning hours of the 17th. Haines Customs measured 13.0 inches of new snowfall at 0700 AKST on 12/17 and 14.0 inches new at 0700 on 12/18. A storm total of around 16 inches was estimated for downtown Haines on the 12/17 by a spotter, but the snow rapidly turned to rain near sea level on the morning of 12/17.

events.cz_name: INNER CHANNELS FROM KUPREANOF ISLAND TO ETOLIN ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow fell at both Petersburg and Wrangell from the afternoon of 12/15 to the morning of 12/16. The Wrangell COOP observer measured 6.0 inches of new snowfall during the evening of 12/15. Storm totals ranged from 4 to 8 inches for this short lived event.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Hydaburg AWOS had a measured gust of 58 KT at 0136 AKST on 12/18. Gusts around 70 MPH were common near headlands on Prince of Wales Island. Peak winds exceeded 100 KT at Lincoln Rock (marine observation ) on the morning of 12/18.

Heavy snow continued into the morning of 12/18 due to warm overrunning. The heavy snow was focused up the Chilkat Highway on the night of 12/17. Haines Customs measured 11.0 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at 0700 AKST on 12/18. Frequent winds to 40 MPH were observed at the Haines Airport during this storm.

A trained spotter in downtown Haines measured a storm total of 5.3 inches of new snow at 1800 AKST on 12/23. 6-8 inches new additional snow fell on the night of 12/23. 8 more inches of snow fell during the day of 11/24. One spotter had a storm total of 16 inches that had compacted.

The Glacier Bay area had quite a mix of winter weather on 12/23. 4.6 inches of new snow was measured at 1330 AKST on 12/23 which was followed by rain and freezing rain. Outlying areas probably received higher amounts of new snow on 12/23. Some wind was reported at Bartlett Cove which implied that the more windy areas probably had wind gusts to 30 MPH as also inferred from NCEP surface analyses.
Spotters measured 4 to 6 inches inches of new snowfall in 12 hours ending around 1800 AKST on 12/23. Gale force winds occurred in Icy Strait just to the north of Hoonah, with some wind inland.

Snow amounts around Haines were highly variable. The deepest new snowfall was downtown Haines where a spotter measured 8.7 inches of new snow for 24 hours ending at 0800 AKST on 12/25. When compared to the Haines Airport ASOS, the heavy snow was during a period of 6 hours in the early morning. The snow started to turn to rain around 1100 AKST on 12/25 for a real, slushy mess.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Based on the NCEP surface observation map, a tight pressure gradient was oriented along the west coast of Prince of Wales Island, the evening of the 27th and into the morning of the 28th. This gradient is typically strong enough to produce gusts of 60 mph or more over western portion of the island.

The coop observer at the Haines Customs station reported that the overrunning snow started the evening of the 15th and tapered off during the evening of the the 16th at their location. Total 2 day snowfall total of 13 inches by the morning of the 17th... with at least 7.5 falling by 7 am AKST on the 16th.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Hydaburg AWOS reported several peak winds in the 60 to 65 mph range through the late afternoon and evening on 1/16.

Thorne Bay coop observer reported that there were downed trees across power lines resulting in power outages overnight on 1/16. There were reports of very strong winds in mid Clarence Strait, gusts over 65kt, that would have been affecting exposed capes along the strait.
A Coop observer reported an accumulation of 10 inches of new snow at 7 am AKST the morning of the 12th.
The Skagway Customs station reported blizzard conditions there and on the Klondike Highway.  Klondike Highway was closed briefly earlier due to avalanche of snow and rocks.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Peak gust measured was at 936 am AKST on the 10th. Gusty winds continued into the early evening.

Haines Coop observer reported the following snow totals at 8 am AKST on the 11th 18 inches, on the 12th 16 i nches, and 13th 5.2 (3 day total 39.2 inches).  Haines Custom station coop reported 8 inches the morning of the 12th (7 am AKST), and 6.5 inches.  Also a spotter near Haines report the morning of the 13th reported a total snowfall over the event of 47 inches.

Gustavus coop observer reported a snow accumulation just under 6 inches the morning of the 11th. By the morning the 12th at 7 am AKST and additional 7 inches had fallen with another 6.2 by the morning of the 13th.  Storm total for the event in Gustavus was 18.9 inches.
The Hoonah coop observer reported a snow fall of 6.3 inches at 9am AKST the 11th, an additional 8.5 inches at 9 am AKST the 12th.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: The Elfin Cove coop observer reported a snowfall of 6.2 inches through 3 pm AKST the 11th, and an additional 4.2 by the afternoon of the 12th.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: A spotter in the Lemon Creek area reported a snowfall of 8 inches for a 12 hour period ending 10am AKST the 13th. A spotter at Tee Harbor and the Auke Bay coop reported a snowfall of 7 inches fro the snowfall. Several other stations reported roughly 6 inches of snow from this event. Colder coop station in interior valleys, like Canyon Island reported a snow fall of 11.1 inches at 8am AKST and Annex Creek Power station reported 13.2 inches at 6 pm.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: The Juneau airport and the NWS Forecast Office picked up nearly 8 inches (7.7 and 8.0 respectively) by midnight the night of the 11th. In Douglas a NWS employee reported 8 inches by 3pm AKST the 11th and a total of 13 inches by 10am the 12th. A coop in Tee harbor reported a snow fall of 7 inches on the 11th.  Coop sites located in colder valleys near Juneau Canyon Island reported 19.8 inches  (24 hour totals at 8am AKST 8.7 on 11th and 11.1 the 12th) and Annex Creek Power Station 20.0 inches (at 6 pm AKST 11.0 on the 11th and 9.0 inches on the 12th).

The Haines ASOS reported heavy snow began roughly around 0500 AKST on 1/7.  he coop observer in Haines reported an accumulation of 7.4 inches of snow at 0800 AKST on 1/7.  Freezing rain began at the Haines ASOS began at 1318 AKST and continued over night to roughly 0800 on 1/8.

There was a massive observation outage during that time, but pressure gradients from NCEP surface analysis were very strong. Lincoln Rock, a marine observation in Clarence Strait, had a peak wind of 52 KT at 1000 AKST on 2/5.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA

Haines Customs observed 12.2 inches of new snow at 0800 AKST on 2/6 and an additional 5.2 inches on 2/7. Haines airport observed freezing rain at times through this period.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Strong winds occurred for the western part of Prince of Wales Island on the morning of 3/1. The strongest recorded wind was at Hydaburg AWOS with a gust of 55 KT at 0416 AKST on 3/1.

On the afternoon of 3/5 Skagway Airport had visibilities below 2 miles in snow. |Frequent gusts above 35 MPH were also observed. A trained spotter up the Klondike Highway at 1400 AKST observed blowing snow and it is likely that white out conditions occurred further up the highway. Several reports of 1/4 mile in snow were observed on the morning of 3/6. More gusts in the 50 MPH range occurred in the afternoon at which point the snow then changed to rain.

The Haines area was hit hard by this winter storm. On the afternoon of 3/5 near white-out conditions were reported by several spotters, Snow accumulated to 8.5 inches by 0700 AKST on 3/6. Numerous wind gusts to 40 MPH were observed though 3/6.

Skagway Customs received 10.0 inches new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 1600 AKST on 3/6 plus 3 more inches new snow during the evening. Strong winds and low visibility were also reported in this storm. See blizzard on the previous event.

events.cz_name: CAPE DECISION TO SALISBURY SOUND COASTAL AREA

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA

Annette ASOS had a peak gust og 46 KT at 1953 AKST on 3/13. Lincoln Rock in Clanrance ST. measured a gust of 75 KT. Ketchikan ASOS had gusts to 43 KT.

At 0700 AKST on 3/23 downtown Haines had received 3.0 inches of new snow. By 1800|AKST a spotter measured 19.0 inches of new snow. Haines Customs measured 15.0 inches of new snow by 0700 AKST on 3/24 and downtown had a total of 20.0 inches new snowfall.

Although Lincoln Rock is a windy marine observation, the extreme winds observed there on 3/27 indicated that it was very windy for land areas. At 1700 AKST on 3/27 Lincoln Rock measured a gust to 85 KT. There were many readings in the 70s and lower 80s. Winds in Ketchikan were up to 48 MPH. Hydaburg near to the area had a peak wind of 71 MPH. There were no reports of significant damage, but minor power outages.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA

Heavy rain accompanied the extreme hurricane force winds that slammed the Ketchikan area. Boats went adrift from moorings. Power was out for hours. Numerous trees were downed due to the wind. 110 KT measured in the Thomas Boat Basin. The airport only had gusts to 61 KT. Trees bent over as never before... from a spotter report.

events.cz_name: CAPE DECISION TO SALISBURY SOUND COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Sitka Airport measured gusts to 77 mph around noon on 10/12. Power outages and downed trees were reported.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Land stations were not available to measure this wind storm. Cape Spencer measured a peak wind of 86 KT (103 MPH) at 1900 AKST on 10/12. Gusts to 70 MPH would have occurred over land around this time.

events.event_narrative: Sitka Airport had measured gusts to 61 MPH on the evening of 10/31. Numerous gusts to 50 MPH were observed that evening.
Along the Klondike Highway up to White Pass, 6 to 8 inches of new snow fell between the hours of 2100 AKST 10/28 and 0700 10/29. Alaska DOT also reported winds to 30 MPH with very poor visibility.

A thunderstorm cell observed by radar moved toward the northwest with a distinct hook echo. Waterspouts were possible under this cell along with wind gusts above 35 KT.|This observation was made around 1340 AKST on 11/1. Buoy 46084 had sustained wind of 33 KT with gusts to 42 KT and seas 13 FT.

Skagway coop observed 0.86 inch of rainfall on 11/1. Frazier Camp on the Canadian side of the Klondike Highway was below freezing the entire time. White Pass has an elevation of 3116 FT. It appears upon analysis and given the elevation of White Pass, heavy snow fell there on 11/1, but the were no official reports.
Haines Customs on the Chilkat Highway received 17 inches of new snow though 0700 AKST on 11/2. Most of the snow fell on the afternoon of 11/1 according to analyses.

events.event_narrative: Douglas boat harbor observed a peak gust of 65 KT on the evening of 11/17. Numerous gusts were observed in the 50s and 60s. A boat was overturned off a trailer.

Snow began at Skagway airport around 0300 AKST on 11/28. It snowed there continuously until 0400 on 11/29. 8 to 10 inches fell on the Klondike Highway between the night of 11/28 and 0730 AKST on 11/29.  10 inches fell in town.

Skagway coop observed 0.86 inch of rainfall on 11/1. Frazier Camp on the Canadian side of the Klondike Highway was below freezing the entire time. White Pass has an elevation of 3116 FT. It appears upon analysis and given the elevation of White Pass, heavy snow fell there on 11/1, but the were no official reports from DOT.

Haines Customs measured 14 inches of new snowfall for 24 hours ending at 0700 AKST on 11/29. Various amounts were measured around the town of Haines with some rain mixed in. Winds to 30 mph were observed with poor visibility on the Chilkat highway. Near white out conditions occurred at times along the highway. This event lasted around two days.
Haines customs measured 4.5 inches of new snowfall at 0700 AKST on 12/4 and 5.0 inches new snow at 0700 AKST on 12/5. By analysis 6 inches fell during 12 hours ending at 1300 AKST on 12/4.
Skagway customs measured 9 inches of new snowfall by 0700 on the 31st. The heaviest snow fell during the night of the 30th.

events.cz_name: JUNEAU BOROUGH AND NORTHERN ADMIRALTY ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Lena Point measured 5.0 inches of new snowfall at 2000 AKST on 12/30. The spotter at mile 17 measured an additional 5.0 inches at 0600 on 12/31. Storm totals ranged from 5.5 to 10 inches overnight on 12/30-31.

events.cz_name: CAPE FAIRWEATHER TO CAPE SUCKLING COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: WSO Yakutat measured 6.4 inches of new snow on 12/29 followed by 4.3 inches on 12/30. Snow changed to rain on the evening of 12/30.

events.cz_name: SALISBURY SOUND TO CAPE FAIRWEATHER COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Cape Spenser had a peak wind of 78 KT at 1200 AKST on the afternoon of 1/14. Although a marine observation, analysis showed that similar wind was occurring over land. No known damage.

events.cz_name: DIXON ENTRANCE TO CAPE DECISION COASTAL AREA
events.event_narrative: Edna Bay spotter observed 7 inches new snow at 1800 AKST on 1/16. Most of that snow fell in the morning. Klawock had freezing rain that afternoon and the peak gust during the event was 34 KT. Nasty couple of days.
Meyers Chuck measured 7 inches new snowfall on the morning of 1/16 and 5 new inches on the morning of 1/17. Ketchikan got less snow.
Hyder measured 2.2 inches new snow on the 15th, 9.0 inches on the 16th, and 7.8 inches on the 17th and 3.4 inches on the 18th for a storm total of 22.4 inches snow.

events.cz_name: INNER CHANNELS FROM KUPREANOF ISLAND TO ETOLIN ISLAND
events.event_narrative: Storm totals for this event ranged from 14 to 22 inches new snowfall.

Snow, wind, wind chill, blowing and drifting snow were the hazards in a storm that hit the Skagway area and Klondike Highway on the night of the 15th into the evening of the 16th. Peak wind of 49 KT occurred at Skagway airport on the afternoon of the 16th and 40s were quite common during the storm. The lowest visibility was 1.5 miles but only a couple of inches of dry, light snow fell. Driving was hazardous in blowing and drifting snow further up the Klondike highway. No accidents were reported.
Haines COOP measured 7.0 inches new snow overnight on the morning of 1/18 as did one spotter. Haines Airport had visibility down to 3/4 mile in snow and peak winds of 26 KT during the night.

Skagway didn't get much snow in this event, but blowing and drifting snow occurred along the Klondike Highway. Skagway airport was closed for several hours with the visibility down to 1.5 SM in snow and gusts as high as 25 KT.

Gustavus measured 5.0 new inches overnight with outlying areas getting even more. Visibility at Gustavus Airport got down to 1.25 SM. Bartlett Cove had peak gusts of 20 KT. Airport was closed at times.

events.event_narrative: Juneau got up to 6 inches overnight based on measurements on the morning of 1/18. Juneau airport had visibility as low as 2.5 SM overnight in snow. Not much wind with this event.
